topic: Wildlife Sanctuaries, Bird Parks, and Tiger Reserves of Uttar Pradesh
description: This topic covers the rich biodiversity and protected areas of Uttar Pradesh. It includes a detailed study of the state's National Park, Tiger Reserves, and Bird Sanctuaries, which is highly crucial for UP state-level competitive exams.

sections.title: Key Concepts and National Park
sections.description: Basics of wildlife conservation and details about the only National Park located in Uttar Pradesh.

key_concepts.explanation: A strictly reserved area designated by the government for the betterment of wildlife and the environment, where human activities like grazing and forestry are completely prohibited.
A protected area where animal habitats and their surroundings are safeguarded from any form of disturbance or poaching, though limited human activities are permitted.

historical_events.significance: Enacted to provide a legal framework for the protection of various species of wild animals, birds, and plants in India.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the first and only National Park in Uttar Pradesh. Upgraded to a National Park in 1977, it is globally renowned for its populations of Barasingha (Swamp Deer) and Tigers.

sections.title: Tiger Reserves of Uttar Pradesh
sections.description: Protected areas declared under Project Tiger (1973) to conserve the endangered tiger population. Currently, UP has 4 Tiger Reserves.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Brought under Project Tiger in 1987-88. It comprises Dudhwa National Park, Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary, and Katarniaghat Wildlife Sanctuary.
Declared a Tiger Reserve in 2012. It serves as a crucial buffer zone for the Jim Corbett National Park in neighboring Uttarakhand.
Established in 2014. It won the prestigious TX2 Award in 2020 for doubling its tiger population within a record time of four years.
Notified in 2022, it is the 4th Tiger Reserve of Uttar Pradesh and the 53rd in India. It is the very first tiger reserve in the Bundelkhand region.

sections.title: Major Wildlife Sanctuaries
sections.description: Important wildlife sanctuaries spread across various districts of Uttar Pradesh dedicated to species conservation.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: Established in 1957, it is the first wildlife sanctuary in Uttar Pradesh. It was originally created for the conservation of Asiatic Lions.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Meerut, Muzaffarnagar, Hapur, Bijnor, and Amroha
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the largest wildlife sanctuary in Uttar Pradesh by area (approx. 2073 sq km) and is famous for the conservation of the State Animal, the Swamp Deer (Barasingha).
It is the smallest wildlife sanctuary in Uttar Pradesh, covering an area of just about 5.4 sq km.
Co-managed with MP and Rajasthan, it is famous for protecting the critically endangered Gharial, Red-crowned roof turtle, and the Ganges River Dolphin.
Located in the Vindhya mountain range, it is primarily known for its population of Blackbucks and Sloth Bears.

sections.title: Major Bird Sanctuaries / Parks
sections.description: Crucial wetlands and bird sanctuaries established to protect both local avian species and migratory birds.

key_associations.extra_info: Established in 1984, it is the first bird sanctuary in UP. It was later renamed as 'Shaheed Chandra Shekhar Azad Bird Sanctuary'.
It is the largest bird sanctuary in the state in terms of geographical area (spanning over 80 sq km).
Despite its name, it is located in UP (not Bihar) and is the smallest bird sanctuary in the state (approx. 1.1 sq km).
It is a designated Ramsar Site and holds the title of the largest natural floodplain wetland in Eastern UP.
Declared a Ramsar Site in 2020. It also houses one of the largest Bear Rescue Centres in India.
Situated on the Yamuna river, it acts as a major hotspot for hundreds of species of migratory birds.

sections.title: Important Facts on Biodiversity
sections.description: High-yield one-liner facts related to state symbols and major ecological projects in Uttar Pradesh.

important_facts.fact: The State Animal of Uttar Pradesh is the Swamp Deer (Barasingha).
The State Bird of Uttar Pradesh is the Sarus Crane, which is also the tallest flying bird in the world.
Uttar Pradesh currently hosts a total of 10 Ramsar Sites, which are wetlands deemed to be of international importance.
The famous Lion Safari Park and Elephant Safari are located in the Etawah district of Uttar Pradesh.
India's first Night Safari Park is situated in Greater Noida, and a newer Night Safari is being developed in the Kukrail Forest of Lucknow.
